title: The Show Must Go On: Marching Bands Raise Hundreds of Thousands After Historic Macy's Parade Delay
snippet: After a fierce nor'easter forced the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to be rescheduled for Saturday, high school and college marching bands across the country scrambled—and raised massive sums—to keep their New York City dreams alive.
content:
NEW YORK — In the wake of a historic postponement triggered by a brutal nor'easter, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is back on track for Saturday morning. But for hundreds of student musicians across the nation, keeping the holiday dream alive meant launching emergency fundraising campaigns to extend their stays in the Big Apple.

Crowdfunded Dreams on the Streets of Manhattan

With thousands of performers stranded by the schedule shift, high school and college marching bands worked quickly to secure extra hotel rooms and alter travel logistics. The Pride of Pearland band from Texas pulled off a Thanksgiving miracle by raising an astonishing $350,000 in under 24 hours to cover extended stay expenses for more than 500 students and staff.

Other groups saw similar waves of community generosity. The Nā Koa Aliʻi Hawaiʻi All-State Band reported raising $500,000 toward its $700,000 goal, while the University of Illinois Marching Illini rallied supporters to cover an extra $175,000 in lodging costs. The University of Connecticut's band will also make its debut appearance at the parade, thanks to swift donations that kept their trip on track. Meanwhile, groups like Tennessee's Dobyns-Bennett High School and South Carolina's James F. Byrnes High School successfully met their emergency funding goals to remain in New York.

Conflicts and Changes to the Lineup

Despite the overwhelming support, not every group could adjust to the new date. The University of Alabama's famed Million Dollar Band had to return to Tuscaloosa to perform at Saturday's Iron Bowl, while financial hurdles forced Macy's Great American Marching Band to withdraw from the rescheduled event.

Even so, organizers remain overwhelmingly optimistic. Executive Producer Will Coss praised the resilience of the talent and crew, noting an "overwhelmingly positive response" as teams pulled together behind the scenes to lock down the rescheduled show.

Star-Studded Cast Ready to Roll

A star-studded roster of performers is still set to hit the parade route on Saturday, including Grammy nominees RAYE, Teddy Swims, and country artist Megan Moroney. Additional headliners include Queen Latifah, Keke Palmer, JoJo, and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, along with a special tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty and an extensive Broadway medley featuring casts from Wicked, Chicago, and Aladdin.

The iconic 2.5-mile parade steps off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, marching down from Manhattan's Upper West Side to Macy's flagship store at Herald Square. Viewers can tune in nationally on NBC, Peacock, and Telemundo.
